exploreItems.title: An existing network
exploreItems.hint: Look for an idea and a limit.
exploreItems.discovery: Spice-producing places were not empty. A new European route would meet societies and trading relationships that already existed.

exploreItems.title: A commercial motive
exploreItems.hint: Look for an idea and a limit.
exploreItems.discovery: Access to valuable goods could promise profit. A promise is not the same as a guaranteed result.

exploreItems.title: A funding question
exploreItems.hint: Look for an idea and a limit.
exploreItems.discovery: Ships, supplies and labour cost resources. Considering a route includes costs and uncertainties, not the price of one spice alone.

exploreItems.title: Name the oceans
exploreItems.hint: Look for an idea and a limit.
exploreItems.discovery: The Atlantic comes before the southern South American passage; the Pacific comes after it on this westward outline.

exploreItems.title: Keep destinations distinct
exploreItems.hint: Look for an idea and a limit.
exploreItems.discovery: Philippine islands were part of the journey, while Maluku was the spice destination sought. Modern labels help locate places, not define past political borders.

exploreItems.title: Read the model limit
exploreItems.hint: Look for an idea and a limit.
exploreItems.discovery: A broad dashed route does not supply exact ship positions, distances, risks or travel times.

exploreItems.title: Landing is an event
exploreItems.hint: Look for an idea and a limit.
exploreItems.discovery: The NHCP Homonhon marker dates landfall to 17 March 1521. Seeing land and stepping ashore are different events.

exploreItems.title: Follow the sequence
exploreItems.hint: Look for an idea and a limit.
exploreItems.discovery: For these selected stops, read Homonhon before Limasawa before Cebu. Other stops are omitted.

exploreItems.title: Limit the claim
exploreItems.hint: Look for an idea and a limit.
exploreItems.discovery: Visiting three places does not mean gaining control of every island or meeting every community.

exploreItems.title: A need
exploreItems.hint: Look for an idea and a limit.
exploreItems.discovery: The marker describes expedition members who needed food, drink and rest.

exploreItems.title: Local action
exploreItems.hint: Look for an idea and a limit.
exploreItems.discovery: People from nearby islands provided supplies; expedition members offered goods in return.

exploreItems.title: What help does not prove
exploreItems.hint: Look for an idea and a limit.
exploreItems.discovery: Giving food is not evidence that a community surrendered its authority.

exploreItems.title: Look at the water
exploreItems.hint: Look for an idea and a limit.
exploreItems.discovery: Low tide and coral limited how closely the boats could approach, according to the account discussed by the NQC.

exploreItems.title: Connect place and action
exploreItems.hint: Look for an idea and a limit.
exploreItems.discovery: The landing party had to cross shallow water rather than step straight from boats onto the beach.

exploreItems.title: Keep the limit
exploreItems.hint: Look for an idea and a limit.
exploreItems.discovery: A simplified shoreline explains a constraint. It does not establish every movement or make one factor the only cause.

exploreItems.title: A communication role
exploreItems.hint: Look for an idea and a limit.
exploreItems.discovery: Enrique helped interpret. A language skill is different from authority over the people speaking.

exploreItems.title: A named event
exploreItems.hint: Look for an idea and a limit.
exploreItems.discovery: Limasawa is the NHCP-recognized site of the recorded Easter Sunday Mass on 31 March 1521.

exploreItems.title: Respect and limits
exploreItems.hint: Look for an idea and a limit.
exploreItems.discovery: Studying a religious event does not require practising the religion. One event does not show everyone converted.

exploreItems.title: Separate voyages
exploreItems.hint: Look for an idea and a limit.
exploreItems.discovery: Loaisa, Saavedra and Villalobos identify distinct expeditions, not one crew changing its name.

exploreItems.title: Departure order
exploreItems.hint: Look for an idea and a limit.
exploreItems.discovery: Read the selected departure years as Loaisa 1525, Saavedra 1527, then Villalobos 1542.

exploreItems.title: Read the date label
exploreItems.hint: Look for an idea and a limit.
exploreItems.discovery: Villalobos departed in 1542 and reached the Philippine region in 1543. Departure and arrival are different events.

exploreItems.title: A demand
exploreItems.hint: Look for an idea and a limit.
exploreItems.discovery: Magellan sought recognition of the Spanish king and Humabon's authority. A demand is not evidence of agreement.

exploreItems.title: A refusal
exploreItems.hint: Look for an idea and a limit.
exploreItems.discovery: The NHCP marker identifies Lapulapu as a leader who refused this recognition.

exploreItems.title: More than one choice
exploreItems.hint: Look for an idea and a limit.
exploreItems.discovery: Zula and Lapulapu did not take the same position. One leader's action cannot represent everyone.

exploreItems.title: A naming connection
exploreItems.hint: Look for an idea and a limit.
exploreItems.discovery: Filipinas is associated with the Villalobos expedition and Prince Felipe, later Philip II.

exploreItems.title: Changing scope
exploreItems.hint: Look for an idea and a limit.
exploreItems.discovery: The name was used for part of the islands before its use spread more widely. It was not an instant decision by all communities.

exploreItems.title: An important limit
exploreItems.hint: Look for an idea and a limit.
exploreItems.discovery: An outsider's name does not create a place's history or establish residents' consent to foreign rule.

exploreItems.title: Identify the sponsor
exploreItems.hint: Look for an idea and a limit.
exploreItems.discovery: A voyage in Spanish service could be commanded by a Portuguese-born navigator. Birthplace and sponsorship should not be confused.

exploreItems.title: Identify the aim
exploreItems.hint: Look for an idea and a limit.
exploreItems.discovery: A ruler might seek commercial access and influence. Different participants could have different priorities.

exploreItems.title: Identify the missing agreement
exploreItems.hint: Look for an idea and a limit.
exploreItems.discovery: A funding document records an intention. It cannot by itself show that local communities consented to the sponsor's claims.

exploreItems.title: A participant account
exploreItems.hint: Look for an idea and a limit.
exploreItems.discovery: Pigafetta travelled with the expedition. His account records a participant viewpoint, not every local voice.

exploreItems.title: A later summary
exploreItems.hint: Look for an idea and a limit.
exploreItems.discovery: An NHCP marker is a modern historical summary, not an object installed in 1521.

exploreItems.title: A classroom invention
exploreItems.hint: Look for an idea and a limit.
exploreItems.discovery: A fictional prompt can help you think, but it is not an authentic historical quotation.

exploreItems.title: A journey
exploreItems.hint: Look for an idea and a limit.
exploreItems.discovery: An expedition can reach a place without establishing continuing colonial institutions there.

exploreItems.title: A later development
exploreItems.hint: Look for an idea and a limit.
exploreItems.discovery: Legazpi's arrival and settlement in Cebu in 1565 belong to a later stage, studied in the next chapter.

exploreItems.title: Control has limits
exploreItems.hint: Look for an idea and a limit.
exploreItems.discovery: Even a settlement does not establish immediate, effective control of every community. Check places and responses over time.

fields.title: First Encounters Evidence Challenge
fields.description: Complete 10 activities: six clue-and-conclusion decisions and four matching tasks. Both parts of an evidence decision count together as one answer. Get at least 7 activities correct to pass. You may read the lesson clues even if you did not save them in your journal.

fields.question: A sponsor hoped to gain access to valuable spice trade. Which clue directly explains this commercial aim, and what does it support?
fields.optionA: Trade access was an aim, but profit was not guaranteed
fields.optionB: Every voyage was certain to make a profit
fields.optionC: Asian communities had no trade before the expedition
fields.optionD: A route gave the sponsor ownership of every destination

evidenceTask.instructions: Read the three lesson clues. Choose the clue that directly answers this question, then choose its supported conclusion. Both parts count together as one activity. You can use every clue without saving it in your journal.

fields.explanation: The commercial-motive clue connects valuable goods with hoped-for profit and explicitly distinguishes a promise from a guaranteed result. Route and landing clues address other questions.

fields.historicalClue: The commercial-motive clue connects valuable goods with hoped-for profit and explicitly distinguishes a promise from a guaranteed result. Route and landing clues address other questions.

fields.question: A report says giving food at Homonhon meant surrendering authority. Which clue most directly checks that claim, and what conclusion fits?
fields.optionA: A supply exchange proved permanent foreign rule
fields.optionB: All later encounters had to be peaceful
fields.optionC: Receiving food made local histories begin
fields.optionD: Providing supplies did not by itself establish surrender

evidenceTask.instructions: Read the three lesson clues. Choose the clue that directly answers this question, then choose its supported conclusion. Both parts count together as one activity. You can use every clue without saving it in your journal.

fields.explanation: The lesson explicitly says giving food is not evidence of surrendering authority. A trade motive or shoreline constraint cannot establish consent in this exchange.

fields.question: Someone claims the Limasawa service proves everyone across the islands converted. Choose the clue that directly checks this claim and the supported conclusion.
fields.optionA: An interpreter could decide beliefs for everyone
fields.optionB: A departure year proves every local response
fields.optionC: One recorded religious event does not establish universal conversion
fields.optionD: Every island adopted one faith at the same time

evidenceTask.instructions: Read the three lesson clues. Choose the clue that directly answers this question, then choose its supported conclusion. Both parts count together as one activity. You can use every clue without saving it in your journal.

fields.explanation: The Respect and limits clue distinguishes studying a religious event from sharing the faith and rejects the claim that one event shows everyone converted. Departure and shoreline evidence do not answer that question.

fields.question: Which clue directly supports the statement that Lapulapu refused the demanded recognition, and what does it help explain?
fields.optionA: A royal place name settled the dispute
fields.optionB: The conflict included a disagreement over authority
fields.optionC: Every leader had already accepted one ruler
fields.optionD: A demand was the same thing as local consent

evidenceTask.instructions: Read the three lesson clues. Choose the clue that directly answers this question, then choose its supported conclusion. Both parts count together as one activity. You can use every clue without saving it in your journal.

fields.explanation: The refusal clue identifies Lapulapu's response to the demanded recognition. Trade aims and a later naming connection do not establish his consent or erase the disagreement.
fields.learningPoint: The refusal clue identifies Lapulapu's response to the demanded recognition. Trade aims and a later naming connection do not establish his consent or erase the disagreement.

fields.question: An exhibit says boats could not approach Mactan's beach closely. Choose the direct shoreline clue and the conclusion it supports.
fields.optionA: Low tide and coral constrained the boats' approach
fields.optionB: Ships guaranteed success regardless of the shore
fields.optionC: The diagram supplies exact positions of every person
fields.optionD: One physical feature explains every decision

evidenceTask.instructions: Read the three lesson clues. Choose the clue that directly answers this question, then choose its supported conclusion. Both parts count together as one activity. You can use every clue without saving it in your journal.

fields.explanation: The water clue links low tide and coral with a restricted approach. That supports a constraint, not an exact battle map or a claim that one condition explains everything.

fields.question: A report claims one settlement meant immediate control of every community. Which clue most directly tests that claim, and what conclusion fits?
fields.optionA: A single settlement proves immediate rule over all islands
fields.optionB: All separate expeditions were one fleet
fields.optionC: The use of a name proves everyone agreed
fields.optionD: Check effective authority and local responses over time; a settlement alone is not enough

evidenceTask.instructions: Read the three lesson clues. Choose the clue that directly answers this question, then choose its supported conclusion. Both parts count together as one activity. You can use every clue without saving it in your journal.

fields.explanation: The Control has limits clue explicitly distinguishes a settlement from immediate effective control of every community. Expedition identity and interpreting do not establish universal rule.
